page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4ms_v2 is a specialized virtual machine instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 168.0 GB of memory, resulting in an unusually high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 42.0 GB per vCPU. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz with 260 MB of L3 cache on Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance provides modern instruction support including AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The hardware profile includes zero local disk storage and lacks bundled GPU accelerators, requiring external premium network storage for persistent operational volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-threaded performance alongside constrained multi-core throughput. The high clock speed delivers top-tier single-core execution, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2351.0 and high single-threaded data throughput with gzip compression reaching 34.8 GB/sec. Conversely, with only 4 vCPUs allocated, parallel processing metrics remain modest, reflected in bottom-quartile stress-ng multi-core marks of 4441.07 and software compilation performance of 5675.0 in Clang. Memory bandwidth operations test in the lower quartiles, registering 36.1 GB/sec on uncached reads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX8-4ms_v2 trades broad parallel throughput for targeted single-core computational strength and expansive memory capacity. By constraining the active vCPU count relative to the 168.0 GB memory footprint, the instance enables qualitative licensing cost advantages for software billed on a per-core basis. It is tailored for workloads requiring vast in-memory caching or high-performance single-threaded execution, such as in-memory database engines, Redis caches, financial modeling, and specialized analytics pipelines.

The server lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier single-core performance, achieving 2351.0 in Geekbench single-core testing and 34.8 GB/sec in gzip compression, balanced against lower multi-threaded throughput due to the constrained core count. With integrated AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, this configuration delivers favorable per-core software licensing economics for memory-heavy databases, Redis caching layers, and high-frequency analytical processing.
